doc.title: Joe Temperley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

title: Junior Mance trio and the Norway recording
summary: He works with Junior Mance; they recorded a Chiaroscuro album on the Norway, and they discuss Mance's tune Jubilation.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Oh, yeah. I work a lot with Junior Mance. We have a new record coming out in the next couple of weeks on Chiaroscuro that we recorded on the Norway, with Keter Betts on Bass and Jackie Williams on drums, Junior and myself. And it turned out very good you know. They just kept recording us every night and we played I think four, maybe five nights on the boat, and they recorded everything. And now they say they have enough stuff for two CDs. So we’ll see. One of them comes out in the next couple of weeks.
Did you happen to play a tune with him called “Harlem Lullaby?”
Well you ask him about that.
It’s a great tune he wrote years ago.
It’s got a real nice sound to it.

No the only thing we played of Junior’s actual compositions is “Jubilation,” which of course was recorded by a lot of different people, you know, like Cannonball and Benny Golson and I think Ben Golson made a recent recording of it. And Jessie Davis made a recent recording of it. So Junior really gets a lot of mileage out of “Jubilation.”
That’s nice to write a tune early in your career that has some life to it like that. Absolutely.
Yeah, he gets a lot of mileage out of that.
